Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

punish verb

also punished, be punished, get punished, punish the guilty

classical

Aug. Conf. 1.9.15
Cic. Inv. 2.66: peccāta pūnīmus (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 196

pūniō, pūnīre, pūnīvī, pūnītum

verb, fourth conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Cicero also uses it as a deponent, pūnior, pūnīrī (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • castīgō, castīgāre, castīgāvī, castīgātum — correct, punish (a child, a pupil); scold

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Quint. 2.2.5; Cic. Tusc. 3.64: puerōs nōn verbīs sōlum, sed etiam verberibus (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    To set right by word or deed, as a parent or a teacher does (Lewis & Short).

  • poenā afficere — punish, inflict a penalty on

    phrase: poena, poenae f. (penalty) with afficere and the accusative of the person · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.18 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 196

  • poenās dare — be punished, pay the penalty

    phrase: poena, poenae f. (penalty) with dare · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 1.15.3; Traupman 196

    The usual way to say ‘be punished’: one pays the penalty. Also poenās solvere, pendere (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • dabis poenās, nōn dīcō quās

    you’ll pay for it, I won’t say howPlin. Ep. 1.15.3

  • sed majōrum nūgae negōtia vocantur, puerōrum autem tālia cum sint, pūniuntur ā majōribus

    but the games of grown-ups are called business, and children’s, though they are just the same, are punished by grown-upsAug. Conf. 1.9.15

  • nam quō saepius monuerit, hōc rārius castīgābit

    for the more often he warns, the less often he will have to punishQuint. 2.2.5

  • poenam dē sontibus exigere

    to punish the guiltyTraupman 324

See also punishment, naughty, forgive.
